div.h3: AI is speeding up software delivery. Now technology leaders need to rethink everything around it
div.p: For consumer and retail technology leaders, the conversation around AI-assisted software development is moving quickly beyond experimentation.

img.alt: Two colleagues discuss a computer lab management dashboard displayed on a monitor in a modern university workspace.

div.h3: Azure Lab Services retirement: build, buy or blend your replacement?
div.p: Microsoft will retire Azure Lab Services globally on 28 June 2027. For universities using the service, the practical deadline may arrive much sooner, depending on their academic calendar, procurement process and change windows. The next step is to decide which workloads to build, which to buy and where a blended model makes sense.

div.h3: The hidden cost of review time in lending operations
div.p: As lending markets become increasingly competitive, operational efficiency is becoming as important as risk management.

div.h3: Listening in at the Leaders Lab London
div.p: Boards are increasingly expecting results from AI, but technology leaders are still working out which bets to make, where to invest, how to govern them and what readiness looks like when the technology changes every few months. This tension shaped the latest NashTech Leaders Lab roundtable in London, where 20 senior technology leaders from across the UK shared their experiences. This article captures just some of the discussion, which may help other CIOs and CTOs navigate the same decisions. Let’s dive into it.
